# Progress M-14M

Progress M-14M (also designated **Progress 46** or **46P**) was a Russian uncrewed cargo spacecraft that delivered supplies to the International Space Station (ISS). Here is a comprehensive overview of what is known about it:

---

## Basic Identification

- **Spacecraft type:** Progress-M (Soyuz-derived cargo spacecraft)
- **Designation:** Progress M-14M / Progress 46 (46P)
- **Manufacturer:** RKK Energia (Russia)
- **Operator:** Roscosmos

---

## Mission Profile

- **Launch date:** January 26, 2012
- **Launch vehicle:** Soyuz-U rocket
- **Launch site:** Baikonur Cosmodrome, Site 1/5 (the historic "Gagarin's Start"), Kazakhstan
- **Docking:** Docked to the ISS at the **Pirs** docking compartment (MRM-2 / DC-1 port) on January 28, 2012
- **Undocking:** August 1, 2012
- **Deorbit/Disposal:** Destructive reentry into Earth's atmosphere shortly after undocking, as is standard for Progress spacecraft

---

## Cargo Delivered

Progress M-14M delivered approximately **2,400–2,500 kg** of supplies to the ISS, consistent with typical Progress-M missions. Cargo typically included:

- **Propellant** for ISS reboost and attitude control
- **Water** for the crew
- **Dry cargo** including food, clothing, spare parts, and scientific equipment
- **Oxygen/air** supplies

---

## Technical Specifications

Progress M-14M shared the standard specifications of the Progress-M series:

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Spacecraft mass (at launch) | ~7,290 kg |
| Cargo capacity | ~2,400 kg |
| Length | ~7.2 m |
| Diameter | ~2.7 m |
| Solar array span | ~10.6 m |
| Propulsion | KTDU-80 propulsion system |
| Docking system | APAS / probe-and-drogue system |

---

## Notable Aspects

- The mission occurred during the period following the **temporary grounding of Soyuz launches** after the Progress M-12M (Progress 44) failure in August 2011. By the time of M-14M, launches had resumed successfully.
- Progress M-14M was one of several Progress missions conducted during **Expedition 30 and Expedition 31** aboard the ISS.
- The spacecraft used the **2-day rendezvous profile** (approximately 34 orbits), which was standard at the time before the shorter 6-hour and 4-orbit fast-rendezvous profiles became more commonly used.

---

## Broader Context

Progress M-14M was part of the long-running **Progress** series of cargo spacecraft, which have been supplying Soviet and Russian space stations since 1978. The Progress-M series represented a modernized iteration with improved systems compared to earlier Progress variants. These spacecraft are expendable — they are deliberately deorbited and burn up in the atmosphere after their missions are complete, with any surviving debris falling into remote ocean areas.
